newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: North sees good uranium demand long term.
newsitem.headline: North sees good uranium demand long term.

text.p: Forestry and mining group North Ltd said on Monday it was optimistic about the demand for uranium in the long term.
Asked at a news conference about the company's outlook for for uranium demand, North managing director, Campbell Anderson said: "I think for long term contracts there is significant demand."
"There is a very good demand for secure supplies of uranium," he said.
North controls Energy Resources of Australia Ltd (ERA) which operates the Ranger uranium mine in Australia's Northern Territory.
Anderson said there were enormous fixed costs associated with uranium reactors and security of supply for nuclear power generators was very important.
A recent pullback in the price of uranium was unlikely to be an indication of further falls.

"I'm not sure if you can have a dead cat bounce off the ceiling but to a certain extent it ran up very quickly and I think there's been some correction as the inevitable trading material has come out into the market," he said.
"The present price is pretty well where we expected it to be a few years ago," Anderson said.
Anderson said the environmental impact statement (EIS) for the proposed Jabiluka uranium mine was scheduled to be lodged in the near future.
The new mine, in the Kakadu national park in the Northern Territory, would increase ERA's uranium oxide production by 1,000 tonnes a year to 6,000 tonnes.
ERA's production is currently being expanded to 5,000 tonnes a year at Ranger, which is 20 kilometres south of Jabiluka.

"We targeted having approval met by the end of this year. We are still targeting that although it has taken us longer (than expected) due to the large number of issues raised from the draft environmental statement. That process has slipped a bit," Anderson said.
North earlier said earnings before interest and tax from ERA rose to A$10.2 million for the three months to March 31, 1997 compared to A$2.6 million in the previous third quarter.
Production from the Ranger mine in the third quarter was 883 tonnes of uranium oxide compared to 163 tonnes in the previous corresponding quarter.
